title: Address on the Situation in Little Rock (1957)
author: Dwight D. Eisenhower
source: Radio and Television Address to the American People, September 24, 1957
citation: Eisenhower, Dwight D. 'Radio and Television Address to the American People on the Situation in Little Rock.' Public Papers of the Presidents of the United States: Dwight D. Eisenhower, 1957, pp. 689–694.

sections.heading: The Supremacy of Federal Law and the Constitution

epigraph.quote: Mob rule cannot be allowed to override the decisions of our courts.

paragraphs: Good evening, my fellow citizens. For a few minutes this evening I want to speak to you about the serious situation that has arisen in Little Rock. In that city, under the leadership of demagogic extremists, disorderly mobs have for days been assembled in front of the Central High School, willfully preventing the carrying out of the orders of a Federal Court.

Whenever normal agencies prove inadequate to the task and it becomes necessary for the Executive Branch of the Federal Government to use its powers and authority to uphold Federal Courts, the President's responsibility is inescapable. In accordance with that responsibility, I have today issued an Executive Order directing the use of troops under Federal authority to aid in the execution of the Federal law at Little Rock, Arkansas.

sections.heading: The Rule of Law and America's Global Standing

epigraph.quote: Our enemies gloat over this incident, using it to misrepresent our whole nation. We must not allow the actions of a few to tarnish our sacred ideals.

paragraphs: The foundation of our American way of life is our national respect for law. In the South, as elsewhere, citizens are predominantly law-abiding and fine people. It is unfortunate that a tiny minority has allowed passion and defiance to obscure the common sense and decency of the great majority of the people of Arkansas.

Furthermore, at a time when we face grave international perils in the Cold War, the events in Little Rock are exploited around the world by enemies of freedom. It would be difficult to exaggerate the harm that is being done to the prestige and influence, and indeed to the safety, of our nation and the free world. Let us return to the calm, orderly processes of constitutional government, ensuring that the law is obeyed and justice upheld.
